criterion: reworked control flow in an existing method (behaviour-preservation risk)
finding: The new rule 'the one in `git worktree list` whose folder holds the `DIAGNOSIS.md` path' matches two worktrees on the default layout: diagnose's `--name` cut lands under `<main checkout>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`, so the main checkout (listed first) also holds that path.
why: The replaced `git -C <folder> rev-parse --show-toplevel` returned the innermost worktree; the list rule names no tie-break, so fix can pick the main checkout and either stop `blocked` on the guard or edit the wrong tree, on every in-repository diagnosis.
fix: Pick the listed worktree with the longest folder that holds the path (or keep `rev-parse --show-toplevel` and require its result to appear in `git worktree list`); mirror the wording in D-21.

finding: A record-only re-run takes HEAD as the Base commit on the premise that only diagnose's --name cut writes an owner record, but the harness WorktreeCreate hook writes one for every session worktree, so a person's session worktree named for the ticket key is taken as a re-run, its HEAD becomes Base, and Phase 7 commits on that person's branch. The Base it records also mixes sources: the old HEAD with today's starting-branch answer, so the branch need not hold the commit.
why: D-20 rejected folder-name detection because diagnose 'would then commit onto a branch it does not own'; the owner record carries the same risk because hooks/worktree-create.sh calls create-worktree --name and the record is written for every --name cut.
fix: Require the record-only re-run's spec folder to hold this Work id's DIAGNOSIS.md, or make the record mark its creator (diagnose) and accept only that; correct D-20's premise.
evidence: +3. ... a worktree record `<git common dir>/afk-worktrees/<work id, lower-cased>.json` ... makes this a re-run. ... with no `DIAGNOSIS.md` there, its branch is the Diagnosis branch, its HEAD commit the Base commit; DECISIONS.md:139 'The owner record still marks a re-run on its own, since only diagnose's `--name` cut writes it.'; hooks/worktree-create.sh:26 `bash "$AFK_ROOT_DIR/scripts/create-worktree" --name "$name" --session "$session"`; live .git/afk-worktrees holds feat-small-lane.json, session-58ecaa40.json (harness session worktrees)

finding: The delta gives a re-run with no DIAGNOSIS.md a Base (HEAD plus the answer) at step 3, but the sibling path at step 4 (branch exists, worktree gone) still discards the answer because 'step 5 keeps the recorded Base', which does not exist when no DIAGNOSIS.md was committed; it also treats a bare existing branch name as diagnose's own, which D-20 rejected for a bare folder name.
why: A first run that cut its worktree and ended before Phase 7's commit leaves a branch with no diagnosis on it, so after the worktree is removed the re-run reaches step 5 with no Base, and a person's same-named branch gets diagnose's commit.
fix: In step 4's branch-exists case, apply step 3's rule: with no DIAGNOSIS.md on the branch, Base commit = the branch tip and Base branch = the answer; and treat the branch as a re-run only when it holds this Work id's DIAGNOSIS.md or the failing test.
